verdicts.reason: The gate plan explicitly makes the crash item's effect the Release Manager's call and requires it be reported as not met (`runs/docs-retrieval-4/06-release-gate-plan.md:93-94`). The resulting checklist follows that instruction and explains the decision while preserving owner override (`runs/docs-retrieval-4/06-release-checklist.md:117-123`).

`retrieve()` raises `QuestionError` for blank or tokenless input (`aveto_support/search.py:457-458`), but the CLI handler omits that exception (`aveto_support/__main__.py:333-347`). Consequently the direct retrieve path at `aveto_support/__main__.py:284` can emit a traceback and exit 1 contrary to the documented exit-code contract at lines 1-4.

The durable request identifies the test but never asks permission to retire it (`runs/docs-retrieval-2/APPROVAL_REQUEST-2.md:9,19-21`); that claim appears only in an Orchestrator-added clarification (`APPROVAL_RECORD-2.md:13-15`). This leaves the specific safety-test retirement unsupported by the request artefact required by `.claude/protocols/APPROVAL_PROTOCOL.md:31-43`.

The owner expressly approved “Anthropic as data processor” (`runs/docs-answerability-2/APPROVAL_RECORD-3.md:1-3`), so INV-5 accurately describes an approval rather than claiming completed vendor vetting. The repository explicitly distinguishes that approval from the incomplete DPA surfacing and UNKNOWN terms (`runs/docs-answerability-2/13-release-checklist-tier3.md:63-68`).

Implementation records an HTTPS fetch of `tokenizer_config.json` (`runs/docs-retrieval-3/03-implementation.md:5-6`), while the approval authorizes exactly two files and nothing else (`APPROVAL_RECORD-1.md:4-7`). The request likewise excludes other repository files (`02-approval-request.md:13,50`); calling the third file an open check did not authorize its download.

The approval record limits the gate change to `docs-retrieval-2` (`runs/docs-retrieval-2/APPROVAL_RECORD-1.md:7`), while Scope explicitly extends it to two slices based on the reviewer’s own reading (`01-scope.md:92,114`). Slice B then relies on that extension without a new owner record (`runs/docs-retrieval-2-proof/STATE.md:24-30`).

The Stages table ends with the superseded tier-2 verdict and partial Docs row (`runs/docs-answerability-2/STATE.md:33-34`), while later tier-3 work appears only in Trace (`STATE.md:92-99`). This materially conflicts with the file’s tier-3 closed status at lines 5-7 and omits the verdict of record.

The intent binds Security to adversarial depth for INV-4 (`runs/docs-abstention/intent.md:72-76`), but STATE admits the Orchestrator reduced it to standard without an approval record (`STATE.md:107-109`). This violates the binding-depth rule, though P1 is excessive because the slice ended NOT RELEASABLE and Security verified the product diff was empty (`06-release-checklist.md:9,15,29`).

`gateCatches` deliberately records defects caught by gates, not the final current verdict (`.claude/protocols/SLICE_STATE.md:147-153`), so its `fail` entries do not contradict later state. The tier-3 checklist expressly treats the six items as blocking landing and authorizes no outward action (`runs/docs-answerability-2/13-release-checklist-tier3.md:11-17`).

The guarded agents invoke bare `node` with no wrapper that converts startup or parse failure into a blocking exit (`.claude/agents/ai-governance.md:7-13`), and the referenced tracked hook is absent from the working tree. The judge demonstrates the required fail-closed form with an explicit `exit 2` (`.claude/agents/aveto-answerability-judge.md:7-12`), which the write-scope commands lack.

The spec requires INV-4 items 4-i and 4-ii to be approved separately (`runs/docs-abstention/02-tech-spec.md:324`), but the only owner wording is the undifferentiated “approve all” (`runs/docs-abstention/APPROVAL_RECORD-5.md:5`) before the documented 438 MB download (`runs/docs-abstention/03-implementation.md:8-10`). The Release Manager relied on an unseen surfacing message (`runs/docs-abstention/06-release-checklist.md:85`), so the record does not demonstrate separate decisions.

The plan requires the later manager to confirm the committed bar was unchanged and says a post-run change voids the check (`runs/docs-retrieval-4/06-release-gate-plan.md:97`), yet the checklist expressly substitutes commit subjects for a diff and admits this cannot exclude such a change (`runs/docs-retrieval-4/06-release-checklist.md:18-21`). No later closure of that evidence gap appears, while the checklist nevertheless declares no failed gate (`runs/docs-retrieval-4/06-release-checklist.md:170-173`).

A pre-slice exact index hash is recorded: slice 3 reports two ingests producing `f36ef5d4...a756` (`runs/docs-retrieval-3/03-implementation.md:19-20`), and its freeze repeats that result (`runs/docs-retrieval-3/04-freeze.md:5`). The release-head hash matches it exactly (`runs/docs-retrieval-4/06-qa-result.md:11`), so the claim that only one hash exists is false.

The durable state simultaneously says the slice is done (`runs/docs-retrieval-4/STATE.md:6-7`), leaves the approval stage “requested” despite the recorded approval (`runs/docs-retrieval-4/STATE.md:21,31`), and labels a fully completed Release Gate “in-progress” (`runs/docs-retrieval-4/STATE.md:24`). Its Updated timestamp also predates the October 8 trace events (`runs/docs-retrieval-4/STATE.md:11,64-69`).

The required proof was that the method SHA be recorded before the fourth set existed (`runs/docs-retrieval-3/01-scope.md:84-87`), but the implementation says the entire run directory remained untracked at the method commit (`runs/docs-retrieval-3/03-implementation.md:32`). Thus `04-freeze.md:3` supplies only a later Orchestrator assertion, not durable git-order proof of when the freeze record was made.
